title: Five-day EP for good-risk metastatic germ-cell tumours
schedule_label: Both medicines on days 1–5 of a 21-day cycle. Four cycles are planned if treatment remains suitable.
schedule_summary: Both medicines on days 1–5 of a 21-day cycle. Four cycles are planned if treatment remains suitable. Days 6–21 have no scheduled EP infusions. Your blood count can still fall. The next cycle starts only after review.
purpose: The aim is to cure a germ-cell tumour that has spread. Each course includes five days of chemotherapy followed by time for recovery.
indication_text: NCCP 00301a covers good-prognosis metastatic seminoma and non-seminoma by International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group criteria. The published indication carries ICD-10 C62 (testis).
administration_text: Each treatment day starts with etoposide into a vein over about one hour. You also receive fluid before cisplatin, which runs over about one hour. Allow extra time for blood tests, hydration and review.
monitoring_summary: A blood count is checked weekly. Kidney and liver tests are repeated before each cycle. A change in hearing may prompt audiology.
review_status: Feasibility build. Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Stops dividing cells repairing breaks in their DNA.
agents.mechanism: Stops dividing cells repairing breaks in their DNA.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse at once if you feel faint, hot or breathless during the infusion.
risks: Infusion reaction or low blood pressure
symptoms: Infusion reaction or low blood pressure
visual: Stops dividing cells repairing breaks in their DNA.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Joins strands of DNA together so dividing cancer cells cannot copy their DNA normally.
agents.mechanism: Joins strands of DNA together so dividing cancer cells cannot copy their DNA normally.
agents.watch: Report ringing ears, trouble hearing, tingling, reduced urine or vomiting that prevents drinking.
visual: Joins strands of DNA together so dividing cancer cells cannot copy their DNA normally.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Tiredness, changes in appetite and nausea can affect meals and daily activity. Tell your team early if you are eating or drinking less.

common_effects.title: At home
common_effects.text: Hair loss and a sore mouth can occur. Ask for mouth care or dietary advice before eating and drinking become difficult.

serious_effects.title: Hearing changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report ringing or muffled hearing before the next infusion. Changes can persist.

serious_effects.title: Kidney injury · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team if you pass much less urine or cannot keep drinks down.

serious_effects.title: Nerve changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report new tingling, numb feet or difficulty with buttons.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Call urgently for fever, shivering, bleeding that will not stop or feeling suddenly unwell.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: During the infusion tell the nurse immediately about tight breathing, dizziness or flushing.

serious_effects.title: Sore mouth · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Report painful ulcers or difficulty drinking so the team can help.

phases.label: Day 1 · begin five-day EP
phases.detail: Bring your medicines list. The team checks your treatment plan and dates one anti-sickness course for the whole block.

phases.label: Days 2–5 · continue EP
phases.detail: On each of these four days both infusions and kidney-protecting fluid are repeated. Show the team your dated anti-sickness plan each day.

questions.q: Can I skip the last infusion if I feel unwell?
questions.a: Call the team straight away. The prescribing consultant weighs any delay against the aim of cure and tells you what to do about the next visit.

questions.q: What happens after this part of treatment?
questions.a: Days 6–21 have no scheduled EP infusions. Your blood count can still fall. The next cycle starts only after review.

Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding or sudden illness, including during the treatment break. Sudden chest pain, collapse or severe breathlessness needs emergency help.

Some germ-cell tumours release substances into the blood. Your team may follow alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), a hormone called beta-hCG, and an enzyme called LDH. They interpret changes alongside your scans.

timeline.label: Etoposide and cisplatin
timeline.text: Both infusions on each of days 1–5, with IV fluid before cisplatin.

timeline.label: Dated anti-sickness course
timeline.text: Use the signed schedule for treatment and the two days afterwards.

timeline.label: Recovery and review
timeline.text: No scheduled EP infusion. Your symptoms or blood tests may need attention on any day.

day_groups.title: Hospital treatment
day_groups.body: Both infusions on each of days 1–5, with IV fluid before cisplatin.

day_groups.title: Recovery and review
day_groups.body: No scheduled EP infusion. Your symptoms or blood tests may need attention on any day.
day_groups.action: Call urgently for a fever or if suddenly unwell.

support.title: Etoposide
support.text: Tell the nurse at once if you feel faint, hot or breathless during the infusion.

support.title: Cisplatin
support.text: Report ringing ears, trouble hearing, tingling, reduced urine or vomiting that prevents drinking.

support.title: Fluids and nausea
support.text: Kidney-protecting fluid is given before cisplatin. Follow your dated anti-sickness plan and call if vomiting prevents drinking.

support.title: Gaps between treatment visits
support.text: Keep your 24-hour oncology number and treatment card with you. Report fever or sudden illness straight away, including at night and during a break.

teachback: Can you point to the next infusion date, show which anti-sickness doses you already took and find the 24-hour number?
consent_support: Discuss the curative aim, fertility preservation before the first dose, possible persistent hearing or nerve effects, and why timing matters.
safety_note: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding or sudden illness, including during the treatment break. Sudden chest pain, collapse or severe breathlessness needs emergency help.

evidence.title: Four cycles of EP in good-risk germ-cell tumours
evidence.interpretation: At one specialist centre, about 94 of every 100 people treated with four cycles were alive five years later without the cancer getting worse. These figures describe a group of people with good-risk disease.
evidence.limitations: Most people in this study had testicular germ-cell tumours. Your own outlook depends on the type of tumour and how it responds to treatment.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before the first cycle
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver function are checked. The team considers a hearing test and discusses fertility preservation, including sperm banking where appropriate.
Raise fertility questions before the first infusion, even if you are unsure about future plans.

rows.label: During each cycle
cells: A blood count is checked weekly. Kidney and liver tests are repeated before each cycle. A change in hearing may prompt audiology.
Keep your weekly blood appointment during the break. Report numbness, ringing in the ears, or a change in how much urine you pass.

rows.label: At response review
cells: Your specialist plans scans and tumour-marker tests according to your disease. AFP, beta-hCG and LDH may be relevant depending on tumour type and earlier results.
Ask which markers matter for you and how any residual mass will be assessed.

monitoring_schedule.note: Your team records the dates and arranges extra tests if your symptoms or results change.
